findings.where: First screen, the supporting line under Mark's heading (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The first screen never says that Mark gives legal advice on PPP laws and frameworks. The heading is an opinion about the field. The supporting line says he advises 'on infrastructure' and on 'PPPs that work as true partnerships', which is vague. Only the small 'Formerly Lead Lawyer' credential in the header hints at law, so the visitor has to work out that this is a legal advisor.
findings.who_objects: The senior development-bank official looking for an independent legal advisor on a PPP law. In the five-second scan they cannot confirm that this person does that work, and the brief asks the page to show what Mark does: law, PPP and advice to governments.

findings.where: Phone, first screen: the order of heading, address strip and supporting paragraph
findings.fault: On phone, the paragraph saying what Mark does and for whom drops below the yellow 'Write to me directly' strip, so the page asks the visitor to write before telling them what he offers. Desktop puts the paragraph first. The yellow strip also stops being the foot of the sheet, which is the idea the tile itself claims for it: a letter's sender address at the bottom.
findings.who_objects: An official reading on a phone between meetings meets the call to action before the reason to act. The paragraph is also pushed below the first phone screen, so the five-second test rests on the heading alone.

findings.where: Navigation (Profile, Articles, Blog) and the end of the article specimen
findings.fault: The navigation has no Contact item, and the article ends with no way to reach Mark. The only contact route is the strip on the home page's first screen.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who lands on an article from a LinkedIn post, which is how this audience often arrives, has to go looking for how to reach him. First-visit trust asks for a contact route as part of the site's structure on every page.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' block under the article
findings.fault: The block is labelled only 'Download' and holds one unrelated 2026 lecture under a 2024 blog post. It reads as this article's own download, not as Mark's list of papers, and a list of one does not show the depth the brief calls 'the product'.
findings.who_objects: A reader who clicks expecting a PDF of the article gets a different lecture. The founder, who wants the PDF list to show Mark's depth, sees a lone link.

findings.fault: The greyscale treatment turns the stage backdrop into a flat, near-black block the full width of the column. It is the darkest, heaviest thing on the page and pulls the eye off the reading column. The brief asks for imagery graded into the house colours, and this grey reads as dour newsprint.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article, whose eye the block pulls away from the text. The founder, who asked for 'alive, not boring' and for photos graded into the house blue and grey.

findings.fault: The display title uses a straight typewriter apostrophe, while the body text uses typographic quotation marks.
findings.who_objects: A legal reader used to well-set documents. At display size, a straight apostrophe looks unfinished on a page whose whole idea is a refined legal paper.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the timing table at phone width
findings.fault: The four-column table squeezes the Element column to a few words per line: one row breaks into seven lines and the easing value splits across three, so the table is hard to read.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reviews the tile on a phone and has to piece the timing back together.
